evidence: All functionality resides within a single codebase (fsdet, tools, demo, datasets) with no separate services or network boundaries
Clear separation of concerns via directory structure (configs, datasets, fsdet/*, tools, demo, docs), indicating modular decomposition
fsdet package provides core abstraction layers (modeling, data, engine, evaluation) with internal dependencies but minimal external coupling
High cohesion within modules (e.g., fsdet/engine contains training logic, fsdet/evaluation contains evaluation logic)
Use of registries and configuration (CfgNode) to enable extensibility while keeping the system monolithic
Main entry points are command-line tools (tools/train_net.py, tools/test_net.py, demo/demo.py) integrated with core modules, typical of modular monoliths
Low average fan-out (4.48) suggests bounded module coupling
No evidence of inter-service communication patterns (HTTP/gRPC/messaging)
Repository depth of 4 levels indicates reasonable nesting without excessive fragmentation
risks: Tight integration between modules may reduce testability and composability compared to hexagonal architecture
As the system grows, risk of implicit dependencies between modules increases without strict layer enforcement
Limited deployment flexibility compared to microservices
No explicit adaptors/ports to isolate core domain from infrastructure concerns
